html:
The Laklãnõ, better known as the Xokleng, are a Gê speaking Indigenous people of Santa Catarina in southern Brazil.

They were mobile hunters and gatherers of the Atlantic forest and the araucaria pine uplands, living on game, honey and pine nuts. When German and Italian settlers moved into the Itajaí valley in the 1800s, the provincial government and settlers paid bands of hired killers, called bugreiros, to hunt them down. Survivors were contacted in 1914 and moved to a reserve near present José Boiteux. The Laklãnõ Xokleng are known today for a land case in the Brazilian Supreme Court, which in 2023 rejected the claim that native land rights depend on occupation in 1988. Their neighbours include the Kaingang.
sum: The Laklãnõ, better known as the Xokleng, are a Gê speaking Indigenous people of Santa Catarina in southern Brazil.
